admin.title: OAuth applications
admin.description: The applications users can sign in to with their account.
admin.forbiddenTitle: You are not allowed to manage OAuth applications
admin.loadFailed: OAuth applications could not be loaded
admin.emptyDescription: Add an application to let users sign in to it with their account.
admin.rotateDescription: The old secret stops working and everyone is signed out of the application.

form.createDescription: Register an application that users can sign in to.
form.editDescription: Change how the application is registered.
form.managedDescription: This application is defined in oauthServer.clients. Change its name, website, redirect URIs, roles, tags, listing and session length there; only the login URL and priority can be edited here.
form.name: Name
form.websiteUrlHint: The origin of the application, without a path. The callback is the website URL plus the configured callback path.
form.websiteUrlInvalid: Enter a full URL, for example https://app.example.com.
form.loginUrlHint: Where the Open button goes. Defaults to the website URL.
form.previewUrlPatternHint: Optional, e.g. https://*.vercel.app, for preview deployments.
form.allowedRolesHint: Leave empty to allow every signed-in user.
form.redirectUrisHint: Extra exact redirect URIs. Public clients may use custom-scheme URIs such as com.example.app:/callback.
form.redirectUriInvalid: Enter a https URL or, for public clients, a custom-scheme URI.
form.clientTypeConfidentialDetail: Runs on a server that keeps the client secret. You get the secret once, after adding the application.
form.clientTypePublicDetail: Runs on the user's device, so it cannot keep a secret. It signs in with PKCE only and may use custom-scheme redirect URIs such as com.example.app:/callback. The website URL is optional.
form.websiteUrlHintPublic: Optional for native apps. When set, users see it and the callback is the website URL plus the configured callback path.
form.websiteUrlOrRedirect: Enter a website URL or at least one redirect URI.
form.isListed: Show in the users' application list
form.isListedHint: Turn off for apps users only open themselves, such as a mobile app. Sign-in keeps working.
form.sessionLengthHint: How long users stay signed in without opening the application. Every use starts the period again.
form.signInAgainAfterHint: Optional: users must sign in again this long after they signed in, however often they use the application.
form.longBrowserSessionTitle: Long session for a browser app
form.longBrowserSessionDescription: This public client signs in on a website, where the refresh token is stored in the browser and any cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw can read it. Keep browser apps at 7 days or less.

credentials.publicDescription: This is a public client: it has no client secret and signs in with PKCE only.
